title: Microsoft separates agent seats, usage, credits, managed objects and one product revenue metric

facts.text: Microsoft said its overall AI business surpassed USD 37 billion ARR, up 123%; the statement did not identify an Agent-only component.
facts.quote: Our AI business surpassed $37 billion ARR, up 123%.

facts.text: Microsoft reported more than 20 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats.
facts.quote: now have over 20 million Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats.

facts.text: Microsoft reported monthly active usage of its first-party agents had increased sixfold year to date, without disclosing the absolute active-user or run count.
facts.quote: monthly active usage up 6X year to date.

facts.text: Microsoft said its Copilot Credit consumptive offer grew nearly twofold quarter over quarter.
facts.quote: Copilot Credit consumptive offer, up nearly 2X quarter-over-quarter

facts.text: Microsoft said nearly 60% of its service customers were purchasing usage-based credits.
facts.quote: nearly 60% of our service customers are already purchasing usage-based credits.

facts.text: Microsoft said tens of thousands of companies were managing tens of millions of agents in Agent 365; this is a managed-object count rather than a disclosed active-run count.
facts.quote: Tens of thousands of companies are already managing tens of millions of agents in Agent 365.

facts.text: Microsoft reported that LinkedIn Talent Solutions agentic products had surpassed a USD 450 million annualized revenue run rate.
facts.quote: have already surpassed a $450 million annualized revenue run-rate.

inferences: Microsoft is operating a mixed commercial model comprising seats plus consumption rather than a single Agent price metric.
Managed-agent inventory, monthly active usage, credit purchasing, seat count and revenue are different measures and cannot be added or substituted for one another.
The LinkedIn disclosure is a product-specific financial contribution; the USD 37 billion AI ARR is a company-wide AI measure and cannot be attributed to Agents.
research_judgment: The call materially improves commercial measurement by separating five layers: paid seats, relative usage intensity, usage-credit adoption, governance inventory and one product-specific revenue run rate. It still does not disclose total Agent runs, total Copilot Credit revenue, Agent 365 revenue or a consolidated Microsoft Agent revenue figure. The evidence supports a seats-plus-consumption transition while leaving overall Agent unit economics unresolved.

thesis_impacts.explanation: Microsoft explicitly described customer service moving from traditional seats toward seats plus consumption and disclosed adoption of usage-based credits.
Microsoft is using its installed seat base, data context, low-code tools and governance products to distribute multiple Agent monetization surfaces.
Agent 365 is positioned as a governance control plane, but the disclosed tens of millions figure measures managed agents rather than active cross-system execution.

alternative_explanations: Credit purchasing growth may reflect packaging changes rather than underlying task volume.
Seat and usage growth may be concentrated in trials, promotions or a small group of heavy users.
LinkedIn agentic product revenue may not represent the economics of Copilot Studio or Agent 365.
unknowns: Absolute first-party Agent monthly active usage and Agent run counts are not disclosed.
Copilot Credit revenue, realized price per task and gross margin are not disclosed.
Agent 365 paid customers, revenue and active managed-agent share are not disclosed.
A consolidated Microsoft Agent revenue contribution is not disclosed.
follow_up_indicators: Track absolute Agent runs and credits consumed, not only growth rates.
Track Copilot Credit revenue, price realization and gross margin.
Track Agent 365 paid adoption separately from managed-object inventory.
Track additional product-specific Agent revenue disclosures.
